summary: The KOKKOS MEAM force kernel never applies the pair scale factor to the forces or the virial: the whole 'if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; ... }' block of the CPU version is missing.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:692-702 reads 'dUdrij = phip * sij + d_frhop[i] * drhodr1 + d_frhop[j] * drhodr2; dUdsij = 0.0; if (!iszero_kk(d_dscrfcn[fnoffset + jn])) { dUdsij = phi + d_frhop[i] * drhods1 + d_frhop[j] * drhods2; } for (m = 0; m < 3; m++) { dUdrijm[m] = d_frhop[i] * drhodrm1[m] + d_frhop[j] * drhodrm2[m]; }' and then goes straight to 'force = dUdrij * recip + dUdsij * d_dscrfcn[fnoffset + jn];'. The CPU original has five more lines between them, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:622-627: 'if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[1] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[2] *= scaleij; }'. Nothing else in meam_force_kokkos.h uses scaleij -- 'grep -c scaleij src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h' returns 2, both inside the eflag_either block at :186-187.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk' with 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 2 2.0': the CPU style doubles both energy and force of the 1-2 MEAM interaction, the /kk style doubles only the energy and leaves the force (and the virial and pressure computed from it) at the unscaled value, so the trajectory is wrong and the reported energy is inconsistent with the forces.
suggested_fix: Insert the scaling block after line 699, using the correct per-pair factor: 'if (!isone_kk(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[1] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[2] *= scaleij; }' with scaleij hoisted out of the eflag_either block.

summary: The pair scale factor is looked up as d_scale(type[i], type[i]) instead of d_scale(type[i], type[j]), so a per-type-pair 'fix adapt pair meam scale' uses the i-i factor for every i-j pair.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:186 'KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]);'. The CPU original indexes both types: src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 'scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];' (inside the jn loop, after 'j = firstneigh[jn]'). The name 'scaleij' in the KOKKOS code confirms the intent. The other lookup in the port, src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:63 'scaleii = d_scale(type[i],type[i]);', is correct because the base uses scale[type[i]][type[i]] there (src/MEAM/meam_dens_final.cpp:34 and :138).
failure_scenario: A two-element MEAM system with 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 2 0.5' (only the cross interaction scaled, so scale[1][1] = scale[2][2] = 1.0): the CPU style halves the 1-2 pair energy while the /kk style applies scale[1][1] = 1.0 and leaves it unscaled -- and conversely, scaling only 1 1 wrongly rescales the 1-2 pairs of every type-1 atom.
suggested_fix: Change to 'd_scale(type[i], type[j])' and hoist the lookup out of the 'if (eflag_either)' block so the same value can also scale dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm as the CPU version does.

summary: The per-atom pair energy tally uses the unscaled phi while the global energy tally on the line above uses the scaled phi_sc, so eatom no longer sums to the global energy when a scale factor is set.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:188-192: 'if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(phi_sc * sij); if (eflag_atom) { a_eatom[i] += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.5) * phi * sij); a_eatom[j] += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.5) * phi * sij); }'. The CPU original uses phi_sc in both places, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:116-121: 'if (eflag_global != 0) *eng_vdwl = *eng_vdwl + phi_sc * sij; if (eflag_atom != 0) { eatom[i] = eatom[i] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; eatom[j] = eatom[j] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; }'.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk' with any scale != 1 and 'compute pe/atom': the sum of the per-atom energies differs from the thermo pe by the unscaled pair contribution, and a 'compute reduce sum c_pe' sanity check that passes on the CPU style fails on /kk.
suggested_fix: Use phi_sc in the eflag_atom branch, matching src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:119-120.

summary: The KOKKOS MEAM force kernel indexes the scale factor with (type[i],type[i]) instead of (type[i],type[j]), leaves eatom unscaled, and never applies scaleij to dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm as the CPU library does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:187-194: `KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]); KK_FLOAT phi_sc = phi * scaleij; if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += phi_sc*sij; if (eflag_atom) { a_eatom[i] += 0.5*phi*sij; a_eatom[j] += 0.5*phi*sij; }`. CPU src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 `scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];` and :115-119 `double phi_sc = phi * scaleij; ... eatom[i] = eatom[i] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; eatom[j] = eatom[j] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij;`. CPU :622-628 additionally does `if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0..2] *= scaleij; }` - there is no corresponding code in src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h (grep for scaleij finds only lines 187-188; dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm at lines 692-714 are used unscaled).
failure_scenario: Any run using a non-unit MEAM scale factor (fix adapt pair meam scale, or an off-diagonal scale): forces from pair meam/kk are unscaled while pair meam scales them, and per-atom energies differ even for the diagonal case.
suggested_fix: Use `d_scale(type[i], type[j])`, apply scaleij to the eatom contributions, and add the missing `dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm *= scaleij` block to mirror src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:622-628.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 07
summary: pair meam/kk breaks 'fix adapt pair meam scale': d_scale is an int view (truncates fractional scales), the force kernel looks up d_scale(type[i],type[i]) instead of (type[i],type[j]), the scale is applied only to the global energy (phi_sc) and never to dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm (the CPU 'if (!isone(scaleij))' block is absent), and eatom uses the unscaled phi.
evidence: meam_kokkos.h:65 and pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale'; pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:299-310 fills it from double scale[][]; meam_force_kokkos.h:187-189 are the only uses of scaleij/phi_sc in the file (grep). src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 scale[type[i]][type[j]], :116-121 phi_sc in both tallies, :622-627 force scaling block.
failure_scenario: Any meam/kk run with a scale != 1 (thermodynamic integration, fix adapt ramp): energies scaled by a truncated integer, forces not scaled at all -> forces inconsistent with energy; at the default scale of 1.0 nothing is visible, which is why it went unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Make d_scale a KK_FLOAT view, index (type[i],type[j]), hoist scaleij out of the eflag block, add the dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm scaling, use phi_sc for eatom, and re-copy scale to the device whenever fix adapt may have changed it.

summary: Per-atom energy (eatom) is always zero for pair dpd/kk on timesteps where per-atom energy is requested but global energy is not, because evdwl is computed only under `eflag_global` instead of `eflag_either`.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:370-379 `if (EVFLAG && eflag_global) { evdwl = 0.5*params(itype,jtype).a0*params(itype,jtype).cut*wd*wd; evdwl *= factor_dpd; ev.evdwl += ...; }` followed by `if (EVFLAG && (eflag_atom || vflag_either)) this->template ev_tally<NEIGHFLAG>(ev,i,j,evdwl,fpair,...)`; evdwl is declared `KK_FLOAT evdwl = 0;` at line 316 and never assigned when eflag_global==0. The CPU base src/DPD-BASIC/pair_dpd.cpp:154-163 guards with `if (eflag)` (i.e. eflag_either): `if (eflag) { evdwl = 0.5*a0[itype][jtype]*cut[itype][jtype]*wd*wd; evdwl *= factor_dpd; } if (evflag) ev_tally(i,j,nlocal,newton_pair,evdwl,0.0,fpair,delx,dely,delz);`. The identical mistake is repeated in the team-policy kernel at line 488.
failure_scenario: Run pair_style dpd/kk with `compute pe/atom` dumped every N steps while no global-energy compute matches that timestep (Integrate::ev_set then yields eflag = ENERGY_ATOM only, eflag_global = 0). eatom[] comes out all zeros instead of the DPD conservative energy.
suggested_fix: Change the guard at lines 370 and 488 to `if (EVFLAG && eflag_either)` (computing evdwl) and keep `if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += evdwl;` as a separate inner test.

summary: pair dpd/kk reads atom->tag on the device in its team kernel but never syncs TAG_MASK, so the device tag view can be stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:173 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK);` (no TAG_MASK) and line 179 `tag = atomKK->k_tag.view<DeviceType>();`. The team kernel then reads it at lines 426 `const tagint itag = tag(i);` and 447 `const tagint jtag = tag(j);` and feeds both into the SARU random-number hash at line 467. datamask_read is EMPTY_MASK (line 97) so VerletKokkos's sync at verlet_kokkos.cpp:438 is a no-op as well.
failure_scenario: Any host-side update of atom->tag (e.g. `reset_atoms id`, tag_extend after atom creation, a host-side atom sort) leaves the device tag view stale; the SARU-seeded random forces are then computed from wrong tags, giving a silently different (and non-reproducible) DPD noise realization.
suggested_fix: Add TAG_MASK to the sync mask in compute() (and to datamask_read), or only assign/use `tag` on the code path that needs it after an explicit `atomKK->sync(execution_space,TAG_MASK)`.

summary: datamask_read/datamask_modify are set to EMPTY_MASK instead of the arrays the style actually reads and writes, violating the KOKKOS package rule and disabling the integrator-level sync/modify.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:97-98 `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK; datamask_modify = EMPTY_MASK;` while compute() at line 173 syncs `X_MASK|V_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK` and line 278 marks `F_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK` modified. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md: "declare datamask_read / datamask_modify ... exactly the per-atom arrays the style reads and writes". Compare pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:98-99 and pair_dpd_fdt_energy_kokkos.cpp which declare real masks.
failure_scenario: Callers that rely on pair->datamask_read/modify (VerletKokkos::host_force_styles at verlet_kokkos.cpp, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:119-121, min_kokkos) get an empty mask; e.g. in the host/device overlap path datamask_read_host stays 0 so nothing is staged into the pinned host buffer for a dpd/kk/host run.
suggested_fix: Set datamask_read = X_MASK|V_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK|TAG_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK and datamask_modify = F_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK in the constructor.

summary: pair dpd/kk uses two different random-number generators depending on whether energy/virial is tallied on the timestep, so the noise realization (and hence the trajectory) depends on the thermo/dump interval when autotuning is enabled.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:229-240: `if (evflag) Kokkos::parallel_reduce(RangePolicy<...TagDPDKokkos<HALF,1>>...)` -> the range kernel draws `randnum = rand_gen.normal()` (line 349, Kokkos Random pool / RanMars), `else { if (tuner) { ... TeamPolicy<...TagDPDKokkos<HALF,0>> ... } }` -> the team kernel draws `saru(tag1, tag2, timestep, seed, randnum)` (line 467), a uniform SARU hash. The two kernels therefore consume different RNG streams for the same physics.
failure_scenario: With `package kokkos ... ` autotuning enabled and neighflag HALF, changing the thermo output frequency changes which kernel runs on which step and therefore changes the DPD random forces and the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Use one RNG scheme in both kernels (preferably the tag/timestep-based SARU in both, which is also decomposition-independent).

summary: evdwl is computed under 'if (EVFLAG && eflag_global)'; on a timestep where per-atom energy is requested but global energy is not, evdwl stays 0 and the following ev_tally writes zeros into eatom.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:370-379; the guard should be eflag_either as in the sibling pair styles).

summary: datamask_read and datamask_modify are both EMPTY_MASK although the style reads x, v, type, tag and writes f, so the integrator-level sync/modify bookkeeping is disabled for this style.
pair_style dpd/kk reads the per-atom tag inside the kernel (SARU RNG seed) but never syncs TAG_MASK to the execution space.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:97-98 `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK; datamask_modify = EMPTY_MASK;` so VerletKokkos syncs nothing for this style.  compute() line 173 does `atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK);` -- TAG_MASK is absent -- and line 179 assigns `tag = atomKK->k_tag.view<DeviceType>();`.  The kernel reads it: line 426 `const tagint itag = tag(i);` and line 447 `const tagint jtag = tag(j);`, feeding line 467 `saru(tag1, tag2, timestep, seed, randnum);`.  Every other array the kernel touches (x, v, f, type) is in the line 173 sync list.
failure_scenario: Any host-side write of atom->tag during a GPU run (`reset_atoms id`, a non-KOKKOS fix, `create_atoms` mid-run) leaves the device tag array stale until the next border comm (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1560 syncs datamask_border).  The SARU seed is then built from stale tag pairs, so the dissipative/random DPD forces are wrong and pairwise momentum conservation (which relies on i and j drawing the same random number) is broken.
suggested_fix: Add TAG_MASK to the sync list in PairDPDKokkos::compute() (line 173), matching the other arrays the kernel reads.

summary: The sin(theta) floor used to regularize the 1/s force prefactor is 1e-12 instead of the base class's SMALL = 0.001, so near-collinear angles get forces up to ~1e9 times larger than the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:188-189: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0) - c*c);` / `if (s < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12)) s = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12);`, and s is then divided into the force at lines 204 (`ff = 0.25*uumin*cssmscc*(2.0+aa*cccpsss)/s;`) and 209 (`ff = 0.5*aa*d_opt1[type]*exp2*cssmscc/s;`). The CPU base uses 0.001: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_shift_exp.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` and :118-120 `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` with the same `ff=...cssmscc/s` at :130 and :138. Every other Kokkos angle style in this group keeps the base value (e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.cpp:34,188 use SMALL=0.001; angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:34,198; angle_cross_kokkos.cpp:30,173).
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/shift/exp/kk with an angle driven close to 0 or 180 degrees (sin(theta) < 1e-3, i.e. within ~0.06 deg of collinear) while theta0 is not collinear: the CPU caps the prefactor at ff <= C/0.001, the KOKKOS kernel allows ff up to C/1e-12, giving forces ~1e9x larger -> 'lost atoms'/blown-up trajectory where the CPU run is stable, and a force/energy mismatch in force-style regression tests.
suggested_fix: Add `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` at the top of the file (as in the sibling styles) and use it for the clamp so the /kk variant reproduces AngleCosineShiftExp exactly.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 00
summary: sin(theta) floor is 1e-12 instead of the base class SMALL=0.001 (used by all sibling kk angle styles), so the 1/s force prefactor near collinear angles is up to 1e9x larger than the CPU style.
evidence: angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:188-189, 204, 209; src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_shift_exp.cpp SMALL=0.001; angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:34/187 SMALL=0.001.
failure_scenario: Near-collinear angle with non-collinear theta0: blown-up forces / lost atoms where the CPU run is stable.
suggested_fix: Use SMALL = 0.001 as in the base.

summary: A leftover debugging printf() sits in MemoryKokkos::create4d_offset_kokkos(), which the project rules forbid in LAMMPS code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:142: 'printf("^^^^^ memoryKK->create_4d_offset_kokkos\n");' inside create4d_offset_kokkos(), with a commented-out sanity check right above it at line 140 ('//if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || ...) array = nullptr;'). The project instructions state 'There should not be any printf() statements or fprintf(screen,...) ... in new code' and 'Any output statements that were added for the obvious purpose of aiding in debugging should be removed entirely'.
failure_scenario: The first caller of this helper makes every MPI rank print '^^^^^ memoryKK->create_4d_offset_kokkos' to stdout, outside the log file and unguarded by comm->me == 0.
suggested_fix: Delete the printf and the commented-out guard line; restore the real dimension check ('if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || n3lo > n3hi || n4lo > n4hi) return ...') that Memory::create4d_offset has at src/memory.h:742.

summary: create4d_offset_kokkos() never applies the n2lo/n3lo/n4lo index offsets its name and comment promise, so every access through the returned pointer array is shifted, and there is no matching destroy for the pointer levels it smallocs.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:151-172 builds the pointer levels with 'array[i][j][k] = &data.view_host()(i,j,k,0);' and returns without any offset arithmetic. The CPU original, Memory::create4d_offset (src/memory.h:739-755), ends with 'bigint m = ((bigint) n1) * n2 * n3; for (bigint i = 0; i < m; i++) array[0][0][i] -= n4lo; m = ((bigint) n1) * n2; for (bigint i = 0; i < m; i++) array[0][i] -= n3lo; for (int i = 0; i < n1; i++) array[i] -= n2lo;'. It also drops the 'if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || n3lo > n3hi || n4lo > n4hi) return nullptr;' guard of src/memory.h:742 (commented out at line 140), and no destroy4d_offset_kokkos exists to free the per-i and per-i,j smalloc'ed pointer blocks (src/memory.h:769-778 has destroy4d_offset for the CPU version). grep confirms the function currently has no callers.
failure_scenario: The first style that ports a create4d_offset() array to KOKKOS and calls this with a non-zero n2lo/n3lo/n4lo (the usual case, e.g. type arrays starting at 1) reads and writes at index-lo instead of index, silently corrupting data or running off the end of the view; freeing the array leaks the two inner pointer levels.
suggested_fix: Either delete this unused helper, or add the three offset loops and the dimension guard mirroring src/memory.h:742-753 and provide a matching destroy4d_offset_kokkos().

summary: The 3d create_kokkos() overload that also builds a host mirror allocates the view with only two of the three extents and then indexes it in three dimensions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:319-351: 'TYPE create_kokkos(TYPE &data, HTYPE &h_data, typename TYPE::value_type ***&array, int n1, int n2, int n3, const char *name) { ... data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2); h_data = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(data); ... array[i][j] = &data.view_host()(i,j,0); ... }'. The n3 argument is never used in the allocation, while the sibling overload without the host mirror (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:287-317) correctly writes 'data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2,n3);'. The body is also internally inconsistent: it makes h_data with Kokkos::create_mirror_view(data) (i.e. TYPE is a plain View, as in the working 2d overload at line 177-197 which uses '&h_data(i,0)'), yet indexes 'data.view_host()', a DualView member. grep over src/KOKKOS shows no caller passes seven arguments, so the template is never instantiated today.
failure_scenario: The first caller of this overload either fails to compile (no view_host() on a plain View) or, for a DualView TYPE, gets a view whose third extent is 0 and then takes '&data.view_host()(i,j,0)' on a zero-size view -- out-of-bounds pointers handed back to the caller as a legacy 3d array.
suggested_fix: Fix the allocation to 'data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2,n3);' and index the host mirror consistently ('array[i][j] = &h_data(i,j,0);'), or delete the unused overload.

summary: The per-atom self-energy term is tallied into the global energy with a 0.5 factor when newton_pair is off, whereas the CPU base adds the full value; with `neigh full` (which forces newton off) the /kk global vdW energy is exactly half the CPU value.
failure_scenario: `package kokkos neigh full` (or plain `newton off`) with `pair_style multi/lucy/rx linear 1000`: thermo `epair`/`evdwl` is half of what the non-kk run and the `neigh half`+`newton on` kk run report.
suggested_fix: Drop the NEWTON_PAIR conditional and always add the full `evdwl` (this term is a per-local-atom self energy, not a pair term), matching Pair::ev_tally(0,0,...) in both newton modes.

summary: update_table is set only in the constructor, so a pair_coeff issued after the first run adds a table on the host that is never uploaded, leaving the device table arrays too small / stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:68 `update_table = 1;` (constructor) is the only place the flag is raised, and :952 `update_table = 0;` at the end of create_kokkos_tables(); the coeff() override at :97-104 never sets it. The sibling table styles avoid this by overriding compute_table: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:508-512 `void PairTableKokkos<DeviceType>::compute_table(Table *tb) { update_table = 1; PairTable::compute_table(tb); }` (same in src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:1294-1298); PairMultiLucyRX::compute_table is non-virtual (src/DPD-REACT/pair_multi_lucy_rx.h:75) so the flag must be set in coeff() instead.
failure_scenario: A script that does `pair_coeff ... ; run 100 ; pair_coeff ... (second table) ; run 100`: ntables becomes 2 and tabindex points at index 1, but d_table_const.innersq/e/f still have extent 1 and d_table_const.tabindex still holds the old values, so the kernel reads out of bounds on the device.
suggested_fix: Set `update_table = 1;` in PairMultiLucyRXKokkos::coeff() after calling PairMultiLucyRX::coeff().

summary: pair multi/lucy/rx/kk marks k_cutsq host-modified only once, inside allocate(), so a later Pair::init() that recomputes cutsq (after a new pair_coeff) never reaches the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:967-969 (allocate()): `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();`.  That is the ONLY `k_cutsq.modify*` in the file (`grep -n 'k_cutsq' pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp`), and the style does not override init_one (only PairMultiLucyRX::init_one, src/DPD-REACT/pair_multi_lucy_rx.cpp:469-478, exists).  The device copy is read every step: compute_style() line 182 `k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();` and the kernels use `d_cutsq(itype,jtype)` at lines 328, 355, 387, 431, 586-587.  Pair::init() fills the host `cutsq[i][j]` (which aliases k_cutsq's host view) from init_one on every run setup, but only allocate() -- called once, from coeff() when !allocated -- ever sets the host-modified flag.  Contrast the standard KOKKOS idiom, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:262, where `k_cutsq.modify_host()` sits in init_one() and therefore re-fires on every Pair::init().
failure_scenario: `pair_coeff 1 1 tab.txt ENTRY_A` / run / `pair_coeff 1 1 tab.txt ENTRY_B` where ENTRY_B has a different tabulated cutoff, then run again on a GPU: Pair::init() writes the new cutsq on the host, but the host-modified flag was consumed by the first compute's sync, so `k_cutsq.sync<DeviceType>()` is a no-op and the kernel keeps using ENTRY_A's cutoff -- silently wrong forces and energies in the second run.
suggested_fix: Override init_one() in PairMultiLucyRXKokkos to call the base version and then `k_cutsq.modify_host()` (or add the modify_host() to a per-run hook such as init_style()), instead of relying on the one-time flag set in allocate().

summary: FixEfield::update_efield_variables() evaluates equal- and atom-style variables on the host through the plain atom->x/atom->v pointers, but post_force only ever syncs to the device, so on a GPU the variables are evaluated against stale host coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_efield_kokkos.cpp:83 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);` (execution_space == Device for efield/kk) is the only sync in the routine; line 158 then calls `FixEfield::update_efield_variables();`, which at src/fix_efield.cpp:504-522 runs `input->variable->compute_equal(xvar)` / `input->variable->compute_atom(xvar, igroup, &efield[0][0], 4, 0)`. Variable evaluation goes straight to atom->x / atom->v / any non-KOKKOS compute on the host (there is no atomKK reference anywhere in src/variable.cpp), and auto_sync is 0 for the whole run (verlet_kokkos.cpp:311) with ModifyKokkos::post_force only re-enabling it for fixes that are NOT kokkosable. The rest of the package does this correctly: fix_aveforce_kokkos.cpp:85 `atomKK->sync(Host, ALL_MASK);` immediately before its compute_equal calls at 87-89, fix_addtorque_group_kokkos.cpp:79 the same before 81-83, and fix_damping_cundall_kokkos.cpp:89 `atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK);` before its compute_atom at line 90.
failure_scenario: GPU run of `fix efield/kk` with a position-dependent field, e.g. `variable ez atom 0.5*z` + `fix f all efield/kk 0.0 0.0 v_ez`: atom->x on the host was last refreshed at setup (or at the last dump), so every step the field is computed from the setup-time coordinates and the applied force is wrong; the same applies to `energy`/`potential` atom-style variables and to any equal-style variable that pulls in a non-KOKKOS per-atom compute.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->sync(Host, ALL_MASK);` immediately before the FixEfield::update_efield_variables() call (as fix_aveforce_kokkos.cpp:85 does). The same omission exists in fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:139-151 and fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:123-131, which should be fixed together.

summary: list->inum is derived by indexing the last work item of the last phase with index h_ssa_phaseLen(...)-1, which is -1 when that phase ended up with no non-empty work items.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:470-471 'data.neigh_list.inum = h_ssa_itemLoc(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1) + h_ssa_itemLen(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1);'.  d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) is overwritten by the device kernel with the COMPACTED work-item count at :652-653 'if (firstTry) { d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) = workItem; ... }', where workItem is only incremented when 'inum > inum_start' (:632-636), so it is 0 for a phase in which no atom got a neighbor.  The CPU base accumulates inum directly instead: src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:112 'int inum = 0;' ... :244 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: An MPI rank whose subdomain holds no local atoms (or whose last work phase has no atom with neighbors) makes h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1) == 0, so the code reads d_ssa_itemLoc/itemLen at column -1: out-of-bounds device read and a garbage list->inum that downstream SSA kernels then loop over.
suggested_fix: Guard the expression (use 0 when the phase length is 0), or better, have the kernel reduce the total inum explicitly the way the CPU builder accumulates it.

summary: Debug fprintf(stdout,...) calls sit inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device kernel (guarded by #ifdef DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS), which is host-only I/O and cannot compile for a GPU backend.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:524-527 `template<class DeviceType> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void NPairSSAKokkosExecute<DeviceType>::build_locals_onePhase(const bool firstTry, int workPhase) const`.  Inside that device function, lines 618-630: `#ifdef DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS ... fprintf(stdout, "Leng%03d workphase (%2d,%3d,%3d): len  = %4d, but ssa_itemLen = %4d%s\n" ,me ,workPhase ...);` and again lines 640-650 `fprintf(stdout, "Phas%03d phase %3d used %6d inums, ...");`.  These are the only stdio calls inside any device kernel in src/KOKKOS.  Project rules: no fprintf(screen/logfile) in new code (use utils::logmesg), and device kernels may not call host-only functions.
failure_scenario: Anyone who defines DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS to debug the SSA neighbor build gets a compile error on a CUDA/HIP build (fprintf is a __host__ function called from __device__ code), so the debug aid only works for host-only builds.
suggested_fix: Replace the fprintf calls with Kokkos-safe printf() (usable in device code) or delete the dormant debug block entirely.

summary: The per-iteration force dot products of cg/kk, sd/kk and the line-search backtracking loop read the device force view without syncing it, and MinKokkos::energy_force() only pushes host-computed forces to the device when force->newton is set or a min_post_force fix exists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.cpp:524-528 'if (force->newton) { comm->reverse_comm(); timer->stamp(Timer::COMM); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); }' and :538-543 'if (modify->n_min_post_force) { ... modify->min_post_force(vflag); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); ... }' are the only places energy_force() brings f to the device.  A force style without a /kk variant has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128) and datamask_modify == ALL_MASK (pair.cpp), so min_kokkos.cpp:469 'atomKK->modified(force->pair->execution_space,force->pair->datamask_modify);' leaves the newest f on the host only.  The consumers then read the device view with no sync: src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:125-143 (dotall[0]/dotall[1] -> the ftol test and the Polak-Ribiere beta), src/KOKKOS/min_sd_kokkos.cpp:51-64 (set_search_direction, called at :126 after linemin), and src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:286-304 (the fh reduce inside the backtracking while loop).  The omission is inconsistent inside the same files: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:180 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK|F_MASK);' before the loop and :432 'atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK);' in compute_dir_deriv do sync, and the damped-dynamics styles resync every iteration (min_quickmin_kokkos.cpp:116, min_fire_kokkos.cpp:143).
failure_scenario: 'newton off' plus '-sf kk' with a force style that has no KOKKOS version (so f is computed on the host and never reverse-communicated): min_style cg/kk computes beta and the TWO-norm ftol test from a stale device force array, while fnorm_max()/fnorm_sqr() called two lines later do sync and see the correct forces -- the search direction is wrong and the run converges to the wrong configuration or stalls.
suggested_fix: Add atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK) immediately before the reduce in MinCGKokkos::iterate and MinSDKokkos::set_search_direction and inside the backtracking loop of linemin_quadratic, or make MinKokkos::energy_force() sync F_MASK to the device unconditionally at its end.

summary: The Kokkos constructor frees the base class's foriginal array but leaves Fix::array_atom pointing at the freed memory (and drops the base's zero-initialization), so any per-atom access to f_ID before the first post_force reads freed memory.
evidence: src/fix_store_force.cpp:36-44 (base constructor) 'nmax = atom->nmax; memory->create(foriginal, nmax, 3, "store/force:foriginal"); array_atom = foriginal; ... for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) foriginal[i][0] = foriginal[i][1] = foriginal[i][2] = 0.0;' with the comment 'zero the array since dump may access it on timestep 0 / zero the array since a variable may access it before first run'.  src/KOKKOS/fix_store_force_kokkos.cpp:40-42 then does 'memory->destroy(foriginal); foriginal = nullptr; nmax = 0;' without touching array_atom, which still holds the row-pointer block that memory->destroy() just freed.  array_atom is only refreshed later, inside post_force's reallocation branch (fix_store_force_kokkos.cpp:70-76 'array_atom = foriginal;').
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all store/force/kk' followed by any per-atom access before the first setup/run - e.g. 'write_dump all custom out.txt id f_1[1]' or an atom-style variable referencing f_1[1] evaluated by a command before 'run' - dereferences the freed pointer block (use-after-free; garbage values or a segfault), whereas the CPU style deliberately returns zeros.
suggested_fix: In the Kokkos constructor set 'array_atom = nullptr;' after freeing, or better: allocate k_foriginal there with nmax = atom->nmax, zero the host side for nlocal atoms and set array_atom = foriginal, reproducing the base class contract.

summary: The Gaussian-charge Coulomb correction is only evaluated when rsq < cut_coulsq (the pair_kokkos COUL_FLAG gate), whereas the CPU base evaluates it whenever rsq < cut_ljsq[i][j], so the correction is silently dropped for pairs with cut_coul <= r < cut_lj[i][j].
evidence: src/YAFF/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp:160-177 computes forcecoul2/erfc2/prefactor2 inside `if (rsq < cut_ljsq[itype][jtype])` with NO cut_coulsq condition, and lines 189-190 add `ecoul += prefactor2*erfc2*factor_coul;` inside the same cut_ljsq test; line 208 `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_coul*forcecoul2 + factor_lj*forcelj) * r2inv;`. In the KOKKOS port the correction lives in compute_fcoul (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long_kokkos.cpp:226-232) and compute_ecoul (line 301-306), and src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:247-248 / 269-273 only call compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul when `rsq < d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)`. cut_lj[i][j] may legally exceed cut_coul: src/YAFF/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp:363 `double cut = MAX(cut_lj[i][j],cut_coul+2.0*qdist);` and coeff() accepts a per-pair cut_lj (arg[5]).
failure_scenario: `pair_style lj/switch3/coulgauss/long 8.0 6.0 2.0` (cut_lj_global 8, cut_coul 6) or any pair_coeff with an explicit per-pair LJ cutoff larger than cut_coul: for pairs at 6.0 <= r < 8.0 the /kk variant omits the -qqrd2e*qi*qj*erfc(gamma*r)/r force and energy term that the CPU style adds, giving different forces and different Coulomb energy from the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Move the Gaussian correction out of the cut_coulsq-gated compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul, e.g. evaluate it in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl (which are gated by cut_ljsq), or make d_cut_coulsq(i,j) = max(cut_coulsq, cut_ljsq[i][j]) while keeping the Ewald part internally gated by cut_coulsq.

summary: Trapezoid-rule endpoint weighting differs from the CPU style when nbin == 1: the KOKKOS kernel halves the single bin once, the CPU style halves it twice (i.e. weights it 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:316-317 'if (k == 0 || k == nbin-1) value += 0.5*integrand; else value += integrand;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_entropy_atom.cpp:269-273 'for (int k=1;k<nbin-1;++k) value += integrand[k]; value += 0.5*integrand[0]; value += 0.5*integrand[nbin-1];' -- for nbin==1 the CPU adds 0.5*integrand[0] twice, the KOKKOS branch adds it once.
failure_scenario: 'compute e all entropy/atom/kk 1.0 0.5' gives nbin = (int)(0.5/1.0)+1 = 1 and the /kk variant reports exactly half the pair entropy of the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU accumulation exactly (sum k=1..nbin-2 then add 0.5*integrand[0] and 0.5*integrand[nbin-1] separately), or reject nbin < 2 in init().

summary: MEAMKokkos::G_gam() is missing the 'gamma == 0.0' division-by-zero guard that was added to the CPU MEAM::G_gam(), so the two implementations can return different values for the same input.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_funcs_kokkos.h:47-52 'if (gamma < gsmooth_switchpoint) { KK_FLOAT G = 1 / (gsmooth_factor_kk + 1) * Kokkos::pow((gsmooth_switchpoint / gamma), gsmooth_factor_kk); return Kokkos::sqrt(G); }'. The CPU original has one extra line at src/MEAM/meam_funcs.cpp:43-49: 'if (gamma < gsmooth_switchpoint) { ... if (gamma == 0.0) return 0.0; // avoid division by zero. For gamma = 0.0 => G = 1 / inf   double G = 1 / (gsmooth_factor + 1) * pow((gsmooth_switchpoint / gamma), gsmooth_factor); return sqrt(G); }'. git log -L on those lines shows the guard came from the 'static-analysis-updates' merge (63fcdb6e5) and was never propagated to the KOKKOS copy; MEAMKokkos::G_gam is otherwise a line-by-line transliteration.
failure_scenario: A potential file with a negative gsmooth_factor puts gsmooth_switchpoint = -gsf/(gsf+1) above zero, so gamma == 0.0 enters the branch: the CPU pair style returns 0.0 while pair_style meam/kk evaluates gsmooth_switchpoint/0.0 and feeds the infinity to pow, so the /kk run can disagree with the CPU run (0/0 -> NaN when gsmooth_switchpoint is also 0). With the usual positive gsmooth_factor the branch requires gamma < -0.99 and the guard is unreachable, so this is a latent divergence rather than an observed wrong answer.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (gamma == static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0)) return 0.0;' before the pow, mirroring src/MEAM/meam_funcs.cpp:47 (and consider the same for dG_gam, which divides by gamma at line 99 and has no guard in either version).

summary: Every FixWall-derived Kokkos style declares V_MASK in datamask_read although none of them reads atom velocities, forcing an unnecessary velocity sync to the device on each wall evaluation.
evidence: 'datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK;' appears identically in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_harmonic_outside_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_lj1043_kokkos.cpp:37, fix_wall_lj126_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_lj93_kokkos.cpp:40, fix_wall_morse_kokkos.cpp:35 and fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47, and wall_particle() syncs that whole mask ('atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);', e.g. fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:100). The kernels only ever touch d_x, d_f and d_mask (fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:101-103,137-158) -- no style in the family reads v.
failure_scenario: On a GPU run where another style has left the velocities host-modified, each wall_particle() call triggers a full nlocal x 3 host-to-device copy of v that is never used; with several walls this repeats per wall per timestep.
suggested_fix: Drop V_MASK from datamask_read in these seven constructors (fix_wall_reflect_kokkos.cpp:36 already lists only what it uses).

summary: TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh is declared with an operator() but is never defined nor dispatched.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:52 'struct TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh{};' and :169-171 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh, const int&) const;'.  grep for 'ShortNeigh' over src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp returns no hits, so there is neither a definition nor a parallel_for using it.
failure_scenario: None - dead declaration only; it misleads readers into thinking a short-neighbor-list path exists.
suggested_fix: Delete the tag struct and the operator() declaration.
